answers.gloss: A node-owned termination point at which a TE link terminates in a particular layer network.
answers.example: The termination point on R1 facing R2 for telink-R1-R2.
answers.relations: It is on i.tenode and terminates i.telink. Unlike i.ttp, it terminates a topology link rather than originating or terminating an end-to-end tunnel.

answers.gloss: The supporting relationship by which a client-layer termination point is supported by a server-layer termination point.
answers.example: An OTN termination point supported by an optical-layer termination point at R1.
answers.relations: It is an inter-layer adaptation/support relation involving i.tp, not merely the server termination point itself. It expresses that one TP supports another across layers.

answers.gloss: The trail-head point at which a TE tunnel originates or terminates.
answers.example: The head of the A1-A3 ODU2 tunnel at node A1.
answers.relations: It is on i.tenode and originates or terminates i.tunnel. It is a tunnel endpoint, not in this model a generic external service-access interface; i.tp instead terminates TE links, while i.tcep represents an endpoint of the tunnel connection within a node.

answers.gloss: An end-to-end traffic-engineered tunnel that realizes a service.
answers.example: The ODU2 tunnel from A1 to A3.
answers.relations: It runs from/to i.ttp over i.tetopo, can have i.tcep connection endpoints within nodes, and may be labeled by i.otnlabel. It is the TE realization construct rather than a purely abstract offered connectivity-service specification.

answers.gloss: An OTN label describing the tributary-slot multiplexing structure used by a tunnel.
answers.example: The TS/TPN allocation for carrying an ODU2 within an OTU4.
answers.relations: It labels i.tunnel and expresses OTN multiplexing/layer structure, including tributary-slot placement of a lower-rate ODU in a higher-rate container.

answers.gloss: An endpoint of a tunnel connection within a node.
answers.example: The connection endpoint for the A1-A3 tunnel on R1.
answers.relations: It is on i.tenode and part of i.tunnel. It represents the tunnel connection's node-local endpoint, whereas i.ttp is the originating or terminating trail head of the end-to-end tunnel.

answers.gloss: A node-owned edge point at which a topological link terminates.
answers.example: The R1 edge point facing R2 on link-R1-R2.
answers.relations: It is on t.node and terminates t.link. It is a topology-link endpoint, not a service-access point or connection endpoint.

answers.gloss: A link object expressing adaptation between client and server layers at a node.
answers.relations: It is at t.node and adapts the layer/multiplex structure represented by t.lpq. Semantically it represents inter-layer adaptation, though my model reifies that relationship as a transitional link.

answers.gloss: A point through which an external client service accesses the network.
answers.example: The externally exposed ODU2 client hand-off at A1.
answers.relations: It is on t.node and provides access to t.cs. Its defining role is external service access; it is not defined as the trail head of an internal tunnel.

answers.gloss: An abstract end-to-end connectivity service offered across the network.
answers.relations: It uses t.sip access points, is realized through t.cep connection endpoints, and runs over t.topo. It denotes the offered service rather than a distinct internal TE tunnel realizing that service.

answers.gloss: A qualifier expressing a signal's layer protocol and multiplexing structure.
answers.example: ODU2 mapped into an OTU4 server container.
answers.relations: It qualifies t.cs and is referenced by t.translink adaptation. It captures the multiplex/layer structure generally; it is not specifically defined as a concrete TS/TPN resource allocation on a tunnel.

answers.gloss: A node-local endpoint of a connection.
answers.example: The endpoint on R1 for the A1-A3 service connection.
answers.relations: It is on t.node and part of t.cs. It is neither a topology-link termination point nor the externally exposed t.sip, although it participates in realizing the service reached through SIPs.

proposals.rationale: Both are node-owned, layer-topology edge points at which a topological or TE link terminates, and both are distinguished from service or tunnel endpoints.
